question:
Due to a major version change, an engineer must perform a software upgrade on a Cisco Nexus Series switch.
Which two technologies should be implemented to reduce disruptions to the network during the upgrade? (Choose two.)
theory: A major NX-OS version upgrade typically requires a disruptive reload of the switch, so redundancy technologies that let a peer or standby device keep forwarding traffic while one box reloads are what minimize the outage. vPC lets a downstream device keep an active link to the surviving peer while the other peer upgrades and reloads, and HSRP lets the standby gateway take over default-gateway duties while the active router is down — together they let traffic keep flowing through the redundant device during a one-at-a-time upgrade of each switch. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 2 — vPC; Chapter 1 — HSRP)
